summary: Bradford Lyman Phillips is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned degrees from the University of Virginia and Harvard, and studied at Naropa University, under supervisors and teachers including David Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, Michael Aris, Masatoshi Nagatomi, and Jeffrey Hopkins.
Bradley L. Herling is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He has held posts at Marymount Manhattan College, attested in 2008, and served as Assistant Director at Boston University.

Braj Basi Lal was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist. He earned a master's in Sanskrit from Allahabad University and trained under Mortimer Wheeler. He directed the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his DPhil under Charles Ramble at Oxford (2002–2006) and his habilitation at the University of Munich (2010–2013). His academic posts include positions at SOAS (2005–2009) and Munich (c. 2010–2018).
Brandon J. Harwood works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015) under the supervision of Patrick Pranke.

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee was an Indologist and historian. He earned a master's at the University of Calcutta and a doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later serving as Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (1975–1998).

Brendan S. Gillon is a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and served as an Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University around 1992.

Bret W. Davis specializes in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Vanderbilt and Kyoto University, he taught and held research fellowships in Japan before serving as Assistant and Associate Professor of Philosophy at Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007, 2018).
Brian Bocking is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 1984), where he studied under Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from circa 1963 to 1967 and studied under Geshe Wangyal.

Brian D. Ruppert works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Willis Stoesz. He held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (c. 1999–2018) before becoming professor and Asian Studies chair at Bates College (c. 2018).

Brian Daizen Victoria is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Komazawa and Temple Universities, later holding posts at Auckland, Antioch, Adelaide, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (2005) under György Kara, and has lectured for the Mongolian Language Program at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center.

Brian Houghton Hodgson was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After studying at East India Company College and Fort William College, he served in Nepal as Assistant Resident and later British Resident (1833–1843).

Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He completed his PhD at Rice University (attested 2011) under Anne Carolyn Klein and also studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies.

Bridget Allchin was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned a PhD from University College London, co-founded the Ancient India and Iran Trust and EASAS, and was a Fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge (c. 1980–2017).

Brigitte Marschall completed her doctorate at the University of Vienna (c. 1979–1984). She later served as an associate professor (außerordentliche Universitätsprofessorin) at the University of Vienna around 1999.
Brigitte Steinmann is a scholar of Tibetology who studied under Alexander W. Macdonald and Bahadur Singh. She held an academic post at the University of Montpellier (attested 2004).

Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland—working with Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop—and has held posts at Auckland, Marquette, and the Australian National University, where she was appointed Associate Professor in 2014.

Brook Ziporyn is a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religion who earned his PhD from the University of Michigan. He taught at Northwestern University before becoming the Mircea Eliade Professor at the University of Chicago Divinity School.
